Dataset Name: cleaned_gene_expression.csv
Dataset Description: source: UCSC Xena - TOIL RSEM FPKM
normalization: RSEM expected_count, then log2(fpkm+0.001) transformed
platform: Illumina HiSeq RNA-Seq
data_type: Gene expression quantification
url: https://toil.xenahubs.net/download/tcga_RSEM_gene_fpkm.gz
dimensions:
  genes: 60498
  samples: 470
description: Rows are genes (Ensembl gene IDs), columns are samples (TCGA barcodes)
sample_alignment:
  clinical_patients: 470
  matched_samples: 470
  note: Samples filtered to match patients in cleaned_clinical_data.csv
data_description:
  values: Log2(FPKM + 0.001) - normalized gene expression levels
  interpretation: Higher values indicate higher gene expression. Values are continuous and log-transformed.
  missing_data: Genes with all zeros or NaN across samples were removed
usage_notes:
- Gene identifiers are in the index (first column)
- Sample identifiers are in the column headers (TCGA barcodes)
- Data is pre-normalized and log-transformed, ready for analysis
- Match samples to clinical data using first 12 characters of sample barcode
- For patient-level analysis, may need to aggregate multiple samples per patient

The experiment faithfully implemented the plan to load all three datasets and generate summary statistics:

• Clinical data (470 patients × 42 columns): reported top 10 columns by missing values; numeric summaries (e.g., age at diagnosis mean 58.2 years, Breslow thickness mean 5.58 mm, follow-up times); and top 5 categories for each categorical column (e.g., gender: 290 M/180 F; primary_site: lymph nodes 212, skin 148).  
• Gene expression (60 498 genes × 470 samples): computed gene‐wise and sample‐wise means (overall mean ≈ –5.44), and confirmed zero missing values.  
• Mutation data (572 902 records × 22 columns): counted 466 unique patients, 19 609 unique genes; listed top 10 Variant_Classification (e.g., Missense_Mutation 311 513) and top 10 Hugo_Symbol (e.g., TTN 3604).  

All steps were executed without deviation and the summary statistics meet the experiment objectives.

Hypothesis: Baseline gene expression signatures can predict the occurrence of subsequent primary melanoma during follow‐up.

Experiment objective: Build and evaluate a predictive model for new primary melanoma events using baseline transcriptomes.

Steps for the programmer:
1. Load cleaned_clinical_data.csv and cleaned_gene_expression.csv.  
2. Filter to patients with non‐missing subsequent_primary_melanoma_during_followup (Yes/No).  
3. Label samples as "Event" (Yes) or "NoEvent" (No) and merge with gene expression.  
4. Split data into training and testing sets (e.g., 70/30 stratified).  
5. Perform feature selection: identify the top 500 most variable genes or DE genes between Event and NoEvent (limma with FDR < 0.1).  
6. Train a logistic regression (or random forest) classifier on training data using selected genes; tune hyperparameters via cross‐validation.  
7. Evaluate performance on test set: compute ROC curve, AUC, accuracy, sensitivity, specificity.

Deliverables:
• List of selected predictive genes and their coefficients or feature importance.  
• ROC curve and AUC value on test set.  
• Confusion matrix and accuracy metrics.  
• Report on cross‐validation results and final model parameters.

{"code":"import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split, GridSearchCV
from sklearn.feature_selection import SelectKBest, f_classif
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier
from sklearn.metrics import roc_auc_score, roc_curve, confusion_matrix, accuracy_score, recall_score
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# 1. Load datasets
clinical = pd.read_csv('cleaned_clinical_data.csv', low_memory=False)
gene_exp = pd.read_csv('cleaned_gene_expression.csv', index_col=0)

# 2. Filter patients with non-missing event labels
mask = clinical['subsequent_primary_melanoma_during_followup'].isin(['YES', 'NO'])
clinical_sub = clinical.loc[mask, ['bcr_patient_barcode', 'subsequent_primary_melanoma_during_followup']].copy()
clinical_sub['label'] = clinical_sub['subsequent_primary_melanoma_during_followup'].map({'YES': 1, 'NO': 0})
clinical_sub.set_index('bcr_patient_barcode', inplace=True)

# 3. Prepare expression data: transpose, map to patient, aggregate if needed
expr_t = gene_exp.T  # samples x genes
expr_t['patient_id'] = expr_t.index.str[:12]
expr_agg = expr_t.groupby('patient_id').mean()

# Align expression to clinical
expr_final = expr_agg.loc[clinical_sub.index]
y = clinical_sub.loc[expr_final.index, 'label'].values
X = expr_final.values
gene_names = expr_final.columns.tolist()

# 4. Train/test split
X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(
    X, y, test_size=0.3, stratify=y, random_state=42)

# 5. Feature selection: top 500 ANOVA F-test genes
selector = SelectKBest(score_func=f_classif, k=500)
X_train_sel = selector.fit_transform(X_train, y_train)
X_test_sel = selector.transform(X_test)
selected_genes = [gene_names[i] for i in selector.get_support(indices=True)]
print(f"Selected {len(selected_genes)} genes for modeling.")

# 6. Train Random Forest with hyperparameter tuning
param_grid = {
    'n_estimators': [100, 200],
    'max_depth': [None, 10, 20]
}
rf = RandomForestClassifier(random_state=42)
grid = GridSearchCV(rf, param_grid, cv=5, scoring='roc_auc', n_jobs=-1)
grid.fit(X_train_sel, y_train)
best_rf = grid.best_estimator_
print("Best parameters:", grid.best_params_)
print(f"Best CV AUC: {grid.best_score_:.3f}")

# 7. Evaluate on test set
y_prob = best_rf.predict_proba(X_test_sel)[:, 1]
y_pred = best_rf.predict(X_test_sel)
auc = roc_auc_score(y_test, y_prob)
fpr, tpr, _ = roc_curve(y_test, y_prob)
cm = confusion_matrix(y_test, y_pred)
accuracy = accuracy_score(y_test, y_pred)
sensitivity = recall_score(y_test, y_pred)
specificity = cm[0,0] / (cm[0,0] + cm[0,1])

print(f"Test AUC: {auc:.3f}")
print(f"Accuracy: {accuracy:.3f}")
print(f"Sensitivity (Recall): {sensitivity:.3f}")
print(f"Specificity: {specificity:.3f}")
print("Confusion Matrix:\n", cm)

# List feature importances for selected genes
importances = best_rf.feature_importances_
feat_imp = pd.Series(importances, index=selected_genes).sort_values(ascending=False)
print("Top 20 predictive genes by importance:")
print(feat_imp.head(20))

# Plot ROC curve
plt.figure(figsize=(6, 6))
plt.plot(fpr, tpr, label=f'AUC = {auc:.3f}')
plt.plot([0,1], [0,1], 'k--')
plt.xlabel('False Positive Rate')
plt.ylabel('True Positive Rate')
plt.title('ROC Curve for Melanoma Event Prediction')
plt.legend(loc='lower right')
plt.show()"}

from sklearn.metrics import roc_auc_score, roc_curve, confusion_matrix, accuracy_score, recall_score
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# 1. Load datasets
clinical = pd.read_csv('cleaned_clinical_data.csv', low_memory=False)
gene_exp = pd.read_csv('cleaned_gene_expression.csv', index_col=0)

# 2. Filter patients with non-missing event labels
mask = clinical['subsequent_primary_melanoma_during_followup'].isin(['YES', 'NO'])
clinical_sub = clinical.loc[mask, ['bcr_patient_barcode', 'subsequent_primary_melanoma_during_followup']].copy()
clinical_sub['label'] = clinical_sub['subsequent_primary_melanoma_during_followup'].map({'YES': 1, 'NO': 0})
clinical_sub.set_index('bcr_patient_barcode', inplace=True)

# 3. Prepare expression data: transpose, map to patient, aggregate mean per patient
expr_t = gene_exp.T  # samples x genes
expr_t['patient_id'] = expr_t.index.str[:12]
expr_agg = expr_t.groupby('patient_id').mean()

# Align clinical and expression by intersecting patient IDs
common_ids = clinical_sub.index.intersection(expr_agg.index)
expr_final = expr_agg.loc[common_ids]
clinical_final = clinical_sub.loc[common_ids]

y = clinical_final['label'].values
X = expr_final.values
gene_names = expr_final.columns.tolist()

# 4. Train/test split
X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(
    X, y, test_size=0.3, stratify=y, random_state=42)

# 5. Feature selection: top 500 genes by ANOVA F-test
selector = SelectKBest(score_func=f_classif, k=500)
X_train_sel = selector.fit_transform(X_train, y_train)
X_test_sel = selector.transform(X_test)
selected_genes = [gene_names[i] for i in selector.get_support(indices=True)]
print(f"Selected {len(selected_genes)} genes for modeling.")

# 6. Hyperparameter tuning of Random Forest
param_grid = {'n_estimators': [100, 200], 'max_depth': [None, 10, 20]}
rf = RandomForestClassifier(random_state=42)
grid = GridSearchCV(rf, param_grid, cv=5, scoring='roc_auc', n_jobs=-1)
grid.fit(X_train_sel, y_train)
best_rf = grid.best_estimator_
print("Best parameters:", grid.best_params_)
print(f"Best CV AUC: {grid.best_score_:.3f}")

# 7. Test set evaluation
y_prob = best_rf.predict_proba(X_test_sel)[:, 1]
y_pred = best_rf.predict(X_test_sel)

auc = roc_auc_score(y_test, y_prob)
fpr, tpr, _ = roc_curve(y_test, y_prob)
cm = confusion_matrix(y_test, y_pred)
accuracy = accuracy_score(y_test, y_pred)
sensitivity = recall_score(y_test, y_pred)
specificity = cm[0,0] / (cm[0,0] + cm[0,1])

print(f"Test AUC: {auc:.3f}")
print(f"Accuracy: {accuracy:.3f}")
print(f"Sensitivity (Recall): {sensitivity:.3f}")
print(f"Specificity: {specificity:.3f}")
print("Confusion Matrix:\n", cm)

# Feature importances
importances = best_rf.feature_importances_
feat_imp = pd.Series(importances, index=selected_genes).sort_values(ascending=False)
print("Top 20 predictive genes by importance:")
print(feat_imp.head(20))

# Plot ROC
plt.figure(figsize=(6,6))
plt.plot(fpr, tpr, label=f'AUC = {auc:.3f}')
plt.plot([0,1], [0,1], 'k--')
plt.xlabel('False Positive Rate')
plt.ylabel('True Positive Rate')
plt.title('ROC Curve for Melanoma Event Prediction')
plt.legend(loc='lower right')
plt.show()"}
